findings.text: Answering point FOUR: this family is not closed. Three further module-level export doubles still decide their own verdict, in exactly the inheritable shape this node removed. VERDICT: MUST-FIX at the family level, reported under follow_ons because all three are outside this node's fence. test_review_release_checkout.py:50 'def _exporter(**kwargs)' returns SimpleNamespace(exported_count=1, all_gates_passed=True, gate_results=[]) with the verdict hardcoded inside the double; test_review_body_authored.py:69 and test_review_release_preview_link.py:53 define the identical shape. inspect.signature over all three reports no all_gates_passed parameter at all (ABSENT), against KEYWORD_ONLY-required in the two files this node fixed. TRIGGERING INPUT: add any test to test_review_release_checkout.py that passes exporter=_exporter -- it inherits a passing export verdict without writing one down, which is verbatim the defect the prior review reported and this node closed two instances of. The detector is one line: all three still carry the comment 'Export gates are scaffolding; these tests exercise ...' that this node DELETED from the reachability double, so 'grep -rn "Export gates are scaffolding" tests/' returns five sites in four files.

A fourth double carries no verdict attribute at all -- the rehearsal file's own pre-change shape, one file away. VERDICT: MUST-FIX at the family level, follow_on. '_export_report(*, total_candidates=220, exported_count=218, exclusion_counts=None, exclusion_records=None)' returns a SimpleNamespace with no all_gates_passed, and it is driven through _RehearsalExporter at :101 into run_review_release with dry_run=True. TRIGGERING INPUT: the same one the prior review named for the rehearsal file -- change _rehearse's dry_run=True to a real cut, and catalog_release.py:2007-2013 refuses immediately with 'Export report is missing required verdict attribute all_gates_passed; release refused because export success was not observed', so five tests in that file flip from asserting accounting to asserting a refusal. This is latent rather than a silent false pass, but it is the instance the aperture most needed to find, because it is the shape the node just repaired.

The verdict this node added to the rehearsal double is inert today, and the per-file count the manifest cites cannot see it either way. VERDICT: NIT on the evidence, not on the code. The test asserts exporter_record == {} with the message 'the export leg must not run on a dry run', so the double is never invoked; I confirmed it by forcing its verdict to False through a self-verifying pytest plugin and getting 5 passed, EXIT=0, unchanged. So the manifest's '5 passed before and after' is true and uninformative about this change -- had the worker written all_gates_passed=False here by accident, the gate would have reported exactly the same five. TRIGGERING INPUT: none that fails today; the requirement is purely forward-looking and becomes load-bearing the moment a non-dry-run test is added to the file. Recording it because the node's own evidence for this file rests on a count that the change cannot move.

The rehearsal double can now state a refusal it cannot substantiate: it supplies all_gates_passed but no gate_results. VERDICT: NIT, and it is the next defect behind the one just fixed. The returned namespace is SimpleNamespace(exported_count=..., all_gates_passed=all_gates_passed). TRIGGERING INPUT: a future test in this file writes all_gates_passed=False against a non-dry-run cut expecting 'Export quality gates failed: <name>'; catalog_release.py:2017 reads export_report.gate_results, the AttributeError branch at :2018 sets gate_results=(), no failed gate is named, and the release is refused at :2027 with 'all_gates_passed=False but names no failed export gates' instead. The test sees a refusal and so may pass on the wrong reason. The reachability double already returns gate_results=[]; a one-line parity fix in the same spirit as this node's change would close it.

Answering points ONE, TWO and THREE for the file the node actually guarded: the property holds at every route, and no site changed meaning. VERDICT: SOUND, recorded as the positive evidence for the node. ONE -- keyword-only is equal-or-stronger than the brief's positional form: both are required (inspect reports KEYWORD_ONLY, no default) and both refuse omission with TypeError, while keyword-only additionally prevents a value landing in the wrong slot and names the verdict at each site. TWO -- the intermediate helper is not a hole: _run_cut at :151 takes all_gates_passed keyword-only with no default, and it is the only caller of _stub_exporter (one call, :165), so there is no route to the double that bypasses a stated verdict. THREE -- the VALUE is unchanged and load-bearing: the double hardcoded True before, both _run_cut sites pass True now, and forcing that value to False makes both tests fail with the production refusal 'Export report has all_gates_passed=False but names no failed export gates', proving the argument is read rather than decorative and that True preserves the prior meaning. TRIGGERING INPUT for the guard itself: call _run_cut without the verdict and the call is refused before any release code runs, which the node's negative control demonstrates at EXIT=1.

justifications.durability: Answering point ONE: keyword-only is equivalent for the property wanted and stronger in one respect, so the deviation from the brief's positional form costs nothing in protection. Both forms are required and both raise TypeError at call time when omitted -- the negative control demonstrates that refusal. Keyword-only additionally forbids silent positional drift: a bare True cannot land in the wrong slot, and inserting a parameter later cannot re-bind an existing site. It also forces the verdict's name to be written at every call, so each site is legible without opening the factory. Answering point TWO: the helper is closed. _run_cut takes all_gates_passed after the bare '*', with no default (inspect reports KEYWORD_ONLY, required), and it is the single route to the double -- grep over the file shows exactly one call to _stub_exporter, at :165 inside _run_cut, so no test can reach the double at all except by stating a verdict to _run_cut first. Three routes by which a default could creep back are all absent: no functools.partial or wrapper, no conftest supplying the name, and the value at both _run_cut sites is a literal True rather than a shared module constant a later edit could flip at once. Three points off for what the shape does not buy. The rehearsal double now accepts a verdict but supplies no gate_results alongside it, so a future test there that writes all_gates_passed=False hits catalog_release.py:2018, gets gate_results=() from the AttributeError branch, and is refused with 'names no failed export gates' -- a second-order refusal that hides the failure the test meant to express. And the rehearsal verdict is inert today: the export leg is never driven on a dry run, so the requirement there protects only a future non-dry-run test.
justifications.evidence: The claimed evidence exists and could have failed. All five logs are on disk. The negative control is genuine and has the right exit class: its first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim ('remove the hardcoded all_gates_passed value from the _stub_exporter in tests/standard_names/test_exclusion_report_is_reachable.py and the file fails with TypeError on the missing required argument'), and it ends '2 failed, 1 passed' with EXIT=1, a test failure rather than a usage error. I did not take the counts from the report: I re-ran both files at the integrated head in my own worktree and got '8 passed' at EXIT=0 (3 + 5, matching both of the worker's revisions; log head_green.log). Because equal per-file counts cannot see a value swap, I measured the point THREE question directly rather than reading it. I forced the reachability double's verdict to False through a pytest plugin that patches the module object pytest collected and asserts that it patched something: both tests then fail with the production refusal 'Export report has all_gates_passed=False but names no failed export gates; release refused because the failure cause was not observed' (2 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1; log probe_verdict_is_read.log). So the value is load-bearing at those two sites and True reproduces the prior hardcoded meaning exactly. The same forced-False probe against the rehearsal file changes nothing: 5 passed, EXIT=0 (log probe_rehearsal_verdict_inert.log), which agrees with that test's own assertion exporter_record == {} -- the export leg is never driven on a dry run. Instrument note against myself: my first probe imported the module as 'tests.standard_names....' while pytest collects it as 'standard_names....', so it patched a second copy and reported a false all-green; I only trusted the second probe because it prints PROBE-PATCHED and asserts a non-empty patch list. Three points off for aperture the manifest does not state: the negative control covers one of the two changed files, and the manifest generalises to both; and the rehearsal file's '5 passed before and after' is reported as evidence for a change whose value that gate cannot observe at all.
justifications.fit: The change reads like the surrounding code. Deleting the comment 'Export gates are scaffolding; these tests exercise report reachability' was right rather than incidental: it was precisely the assertion the change falsifies, and the replacement states the mechanism in the file's own register. Keyword form at the call sites matches how every other injected double in these files is configured. Three points off for two fit costs the report does not name. First, the SPEC was marked exact and specified the positional form; the worker chose keyword-only without recording the deviation in its manifest, which is a reporting miss even though the choice is defensible and I judge it stronger. Second, it leaves the repo with two conventions for the same thing: the largest sibling in this family, test_review_release.py:55, was given 'def _stub_exporter(record, all_gates_passed)' -- POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD, required -- by the preceding node in the same wave, so three files that a future author will read together now spell one requirement two ways. Either spelling is fine; choosing per file is the cost.

Verified at the integrated head 44650230c by a marker the change INTRODUCED, not by the absence of the old form: inspect.signature over the modules pytest itself imports reports all_gates_passed as KEYWORD_ONLY with no default in test_exclusion_report_is_reachable._stub_exporter, in that file's _run_cut helper, and in test_release_rehearsal_writes_nothing._stub_exporter. The two starting states the brief names are both confirmed from the diff: the reachability double hardcoded all_gates_passed=True at the old :110, and the rehearsal double returned SimpleNamespace(exported_count=...) with no verdict attribute. Both are closed. Answering point FOUR, however, the family is NOT closed and the node's manifest records follow_ons: none. Four further export doubles still decide their own verdict, three of them in exactly the inheritable module-level shape this node removed: test_review_release_checkout.py:50 _exporter, test_review_body_authored.py:69 _exporter and test_review_release_preview_link.py:53 _exporter each hardcode all_gates_passed=True inside the double; test_release_rehearsal_accounting.py:81 _export_report carries no verdict attribute at all, which is the rehearsal file's own pre-change shape. The decisive aperture point is textual: the comment 'Export gates are scaffolding; these tests exercise ...' that this node DELETED from the reachability file survives at five sites in four other files, so a one-line grep over tests/ finds the whole family where reading siblings found two of it. Minus two, for the closure claim rather than for the code.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exact. Declared write paths were the two test files plus docs/plans/unbound-source-backlog.html and docs/evidence/archive/unbound-source-backlog-landed.html. 'git show b170033157 --stat' reports exactly the two test files, 23 insertions and 10 deletions; the two documents land separately in e159b4b059 (62 insertions, no code). No production file was touched -- imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py and export.py are untouched by both commits, which matters here because the verdict consumers live there. No assertion, fixture or conftest was added or changed, as the commit body claims. The four sibling doubles named under goal_fidelity were correctly left alone rather than swept in: each file defines its own double, so there is no import route by which this node's required parameter could have reached them without widening the fence. Both commits are conventional with a body, carry no AI attribution, and name no plan, sprint or ticket identifier in the message, the symbols or the comments -- the replacement comment states the mechanism ('the verdict is supplied by the caller, never defaulted here'). Full marks.
